title: github-egress policy (v1)
description: The machine/runner-owned GitHub-egress policy document. Contract 4 of infra/github-proxy/README.md, in machine-readable form. Lives OUTSIDE any checkout (default /etc/2am/github-egress/policy.json); a repo-local copy is a development fixture, never the authority. Carries no secret: credentials are named by external reference only. Versioned and renamed by the same-change rule in README.md.

schemaVersion.description: Policy schema major version. A consumer that does not recognise the value MUST report verification incomplete (exit 2), never 'aligned'.

policyEpoch.description: Monotonic counter bumped on every policy change. Cache invalidation key for the hot local assertion, and part of a P6 cache partition key.

deployment.description: Free-form label for the deployment this policy belongs to (e.g. '2am-fleet'). Attribution only; never an authorization input.

logicalHost.description: The LOGICAL GitHub host: repository identity, login, git remotes and web URLs. 'github.com' for this deployment. GH_HOST is compared against THIS, never against apiOrigin -- see README.md Contract 4.

apiOrigin.description: The mandated REST/GraphQL destination origin. HTTPS only. The expected gh `api_host` is this URL's bare hostname -- api_host cannot carry a port, so an apiOrigin with a non-443 port is only usable by SDK facades and the managed adapter, not by stock gh.

gitOrigin.description: Git transport destination and its rollout state, tracked separately from API routing: git operations are NOT covered by api_host (upstream docs/api-host.md Scope). Pending qualification stays visible rather than being implied by the API rollout.

host.description: Qualified Git transport host, or null while none is qualified.

rollout.description: unqualified: no destination serves the protocol yet -- do NOT install insteadOf rewrites. qualified: destination serves it, rewrites may be installed but absence is not a finding. enforced: missing or overriding rewrites ARE a finding.

allowedDirectEgress.description: Identities permitted direct GitHub API egress -- the gateway's own upstream transport and nothing else (README.md Contract 1, 'sole direct egress'). An empty array means no exception on this machine.

toolchain.description: Approved toolchain identity. Version pins here are ROUTING CONTROLS, not hygiene: below the gh api_host floor, api_host is a silent no-op (see README.md 'Verified findings').

ghMinimumVersion.description: Lowest gh version whose api_host setting actually routes requests. Below this, a set api_host is accepted and echoed back by `gh config get` while traffic still goes to the canonical API.

ghPinnedVersion.description: The exact upstream gh version this deployment provisions and qualifies against.

launcherPath.description: Absolute path of the managed executable named `gh` (P2). The name stays `gh` by decision -- README.md 'Keep the command name gh'.

upstreamGhPath.description: Absolute private implementation path of the pinned upstream gh binary the launcher execs.

upstreamGhSha256.description: Checksum of the pinned upstream binary, or null before provisioning.

sdkPins.description: Approved SDK/library versions per language facade (P3). Keys are facade ids; values are version specifiers.

api.description: required: a managed API workload MUST route through apiOrigin and a routing failure blocks the operation. observe: findings are reported but do not block (migration cohorts only -- README.md 'observe-only cohorts are not the completed mandate').

runtimeEgress.description: State of the host/runner network policy that blocks direct GitHub API egress. 'unverified' is the honest default: config assertions alone can never report enforcement as verified (README.md Contract 4 check 4).

negativeCanary.description: Command the validator runs under the caller's own identity to prove direct egress is blocked. Null means the runtime boundary is unverifiable here -- doctor reports verification incomplete (exit 2) rather than aligned.

principal.description: WHICH external credential profile this machine presents. Never an inline secret -- a policy document carrying a token is invalid by construction.

profile.description: The authenticated gateway profile class. Matches README.md Contract 2's four profiles.

credentialRef.description: External reference resolving to the proxy credential (file path, keychain item, secret manager URI). Must not look like a token.

ghConfigDirs.description: Every GH_CONFIG_DIR profile the validator must check. A profile absent from this list that is active at runtime is a SHADOWED PROFILE finding -- verified live: a shadowing GH_CONFIG_DIR silently supplies its own token and the operator profile is never consulted.

adapter.description: Managed gh launcher / request-adapter knobs (P2). All optional. NOT routing controls: the adapter only ever connects to github.apiOrigin.

upstreamUnixSocket.description: QUALIFICATION ONLY: dial the gateway over this Unix socket instead of TCP/TLS (hermetic fixtures, mock-contract development). Absent in production. Machine-owned like the rest of the policy, so a caller cannot redirect the adapter with its environment.

outcomeLog.description: Absolute path of an append-only JSONL file the adapter writes one client-outcome record to per request (method, api kind, authorities, status, outcome, duration, trace id). Never paths, queries, bodies or headers (Contract 3 content boundary). Null or absent disables; OTLP export is a follow-up.

requestTimeoutSeconds.description: Per-request upstream timeout in seconds. Default 60.

telemetry.description: Delivery readiness, reported SEPARATELY from routing: a sink outage must never switch routing off.
